detailed_description: cURL Converter parses a basic curl request and generates a template in JavaScript (fetch), Python (requests), PHP (cURL), Go (net/http), or Java (HttpClient). Common inputs are the URL, -X method, -H headers, and -d/--data body; a body without an explicit -X uses POST. Quoted repeated spaces are preserved, and generators distinguish JSON from plain-text bodies. Conversion runs in the browser without executing the command or sending the generated API request. This is not a complete shell or curl emulator: cookies, uploads, multipart, basic auth, certificates, redirects and -G query handling are outside the verified scope and may be ignored. Review the code manually; arbitrary commands are not guaranteed to produce equivalent requests.
usage_steps: Paste a curl command into the textarea, including the URL and any `-X`, `-H`, or `-d` flags.
Pick an output language from the dropdown: JavaScript, Python, PHP, Go, or Java.
Click Convert to generate the request code from the parsed method, headers, and body.
Review the generated code in the output panel.
Click Copy Code to copy the snippet to your clipboard for manual review.
usage_examples: Convert a simple `curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{...}'` command into a JavaScript `fetch` snippet.
Generate a Python `requests` call from a curl command with a Bearer authorization header.
Translate a GET request with custom headers into a Go `net/http` example.
Produce a Java `HttpClient` snippet from a curl POST as a starting point before manual edits.

faqs.question: Is the cURL Converter free?
faqs.answer: Yes. The converter is completely free with no signup, and there is no limit on how many commands you can convert.

faqs.question: Is it safe to paste curl commands here?
faqs.answer: Yes. Parsing and code generation run entirely in your browser — the command is never uploaded to any server, so tokens in Authorization headers stay on your device.

faqs.question: Which curl flags are supported?
faqs.answer: The parser reads the request URL, the `-X` method flag, `-H` headers, and `-d` or `--data` bodies. Cookies, file uploads, multipart forms, basic auth and redirect flags are outside the current scope.

faqs.question: Which output languages can I choose?
faqs.answer: You can convert a curl command into JavaScript (fetch), Python (requests), PHP (curl_setopt), Go (net/http), or Java (java.net.http) snippets.

faqs.question: Can I use the generated code directly in production?
faqs.answer: Treat the output as a starting template. It covers the basic request shape — review timeouts, error handling and authentication for your environment before shipping.
